C-RUN-LEDGER.Summary: Give a change bundle durable position and a durable record of what cannot be re-derived: an append-only run ledger, a regenerable cursor, and a cursor subcommand that recovers rather than blocks.
C-RUN-LEDGER.Problem:
A change bundle has no durable position and no record of the facts D1 lists as unrecoverable — who approved what against which evidence, overrides applied despite a finding, degradations where a mechanism reported not-run, and retry budget consumed. Nothing else in the tree records them, so losing them is silent. Position cannot live in plan.xml: a per-task status attribute is schema-illegal (artifact.forbidden-status-attribute) and co-locating position with the plan reintroduces the v3 read cost (D1, F3).
Companion registration does not admit the file. NGRACE_CHANGE_COMPANION_TAGS (artifact/types.ts:28) feeds only the root-tag check in validateChangeDesignContextArtifact (grammar.ts:585); the file design-context.xml is admitted by three separate literals (grammar.ts:751, :798, :809). Adding entries to that constant changes nothing, and a bundle carrying run-ledger.xml errors today with change.unexpected-file — reproduced against the real CLI at 7388d5e (A10.2).
Task IDs collide across bundles by construction: ANCHOR_PATTERNS.task is /^T-[0-9]{3}$/ (artifact/types.ts:98) and every plan starts at T-001 (C-ABSENCE-VALUE carries T-001..T-005; examples carries T-001..T-002). So cursor.unknown-task cannot detect a cursor copied from another bundle, and a stale cursor validates clean while reporting a position that was never true (A11.4).
The graph does not cover this phase: src/artifact/types.ts and src/grace.ts are in no module, and src/grace-cursor.ts will not be — A5.7's recorded finding arriving in practice (A11.7).

Goals.Goal: Append-only run-ledger.xml as the truth: one Epoch-N section per fold, carrying the plan-side wave as an attribute. Epoch-N is structural sequencing and must not enter ANCHOR_PATTERNS (D3, §3.4).
Immutable per-event files under run/ during an open epoch, identified by pre-allocated disjoint ID ranges recorded in the epoch's opening event. No clock in identity or ordering (D2).
Fold at epoch close with write, verify, then delete ordering — never delete first. An interrupted fold leaves both forms and a re-fold is idempotent (D3).
Regenerable run.xml cursor: a fold over the ledger, optional for a project to have, non-fatal to lose, and never authoritative (D1, anti-pattern 7).
One derived bundle-filename constant beside NGRACE_CHANGE_COMPANION_TAGS, read by all three grammar.ts sites, so a companion cannot be half-registered (A11.1).
Required bundle identity on both artifacts, cross-checked against the directory, restoring the convention spec, plan and design-context already follow (A11.4).
src/grace-cursor.ts as the sole write surface, with six subcommands: show, regenerate, advance, pause, resume, fold. show and bare regenerate do not write (A11.5).
Regeneration reads three sources in order of authority — ledger, loose run/ events, then codebase evidence — with row 3 output labelled inferred and never merged flat into rows 1-2 (A11.5).

lint reports, the mechanism recovers: a missing, identity-less or mismatched cursor is a lint error and never blocks cursor show, which re-derives and announces the degradation through Phase 2's verdict vocabulary (A11.5, anti-pattern 9, invariant 3).
Epoch and task counts surfaced in ngrace status without the cursor reaching chooseNextAction (A10.8).
M-CURSOR, M-ARTIFACT-TYPES and M-CLI added to the graph with matching V-M-* entries (A11.7).

Constraints.Constraint: Additive only. A .ngrace tree with no ledger and no cursor lints clean — no issue, no migration (D1, invariant 5).
No timestamps in event identity or ordering. A test that sorts by time is a defect in the test (D2, §0.2, anti-pattern 6).
Epoch-N must not be added to ANCHOR_PATTERNS. It is structural sequencing, not a semantic family (§3.4).
The cursor is never authoritative. chooseNextAction stays derived from spec and plan status and integrity (D1, anti-pattern 7).
Fold ordering is write, verify, then delete. The delete step must be unreachable before the verify step (D3, §3.7 gate 4).
Only advance, pause, resume and fold write. show and bare regenerate leave the tree byte-identical; regenerate writes solely under --apply (invariant 8, A11.5).
lint does not walk run/. Event validation belongs to the fold, and the no-issue behaviour is pinned by a test (A11.2).
All twelve codes are defects. None carries issueClass "absence" — a malformed ledger is malformed, not missing (A11.3, A8).
No doctor flags and no doctor repair. doctor is pinned strictly read-only by scale-ergonomics.test.ts:213 (A11.6, A5.2 §2).
Degradation reports reuse skills/ngrace/ngrace-cli/references/verdicts.md. Phase 3 does not invent a second vocabulary (D13, anti-pattern 5 and 10).
Every authored path resolves through resolveContainedProjectPath (artifact/paths.ts:92). fold deletes files and is the phase's one destructive operation.
No new runtime dependencies. No Phase 4+ constructs: no attempt log, no fix budget, no gates, no confidence field.
skills/ngrace/* is source of truth; plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/* stays byte-identical in the same commit (invariant 1, §12.2).
Shared test helpers live in src/test-support/; src/grace-cursor.ts must not import them (invariant 7).
AffectedAreas derives from the traced code path and A11.7, never from §3.3's provisional file table (A5.6).

NonGoals.NonGoal: Attempt log, fix budget, escalation (Phase 4); gates and the transition surface (Phase 5); reviewer automation (Phase 6).
Confidence recording or the calibration report (Phase 9).
The doctor cursor report line and the analysisIssues rename (Phase 10; A7.4, A11.6).
Lint validation of loose run/ event files (A11.2; the fold owns it).
Repairing code-versus-artifact divergence. That is a replan through $ngrace-refresh, already shipped at grace-status.ts:177 (A11.6).
The file-to-module ObservedWriteScope cross-check (A5.7; still unowned).
Adding Epoch-N or event IDs to the semantic anchor families.
A cursor surviving in an archived bundle as its own issue code (adjacent to the unowned archive precondition; decide once, whole).

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-BUNDLE-FILE-ALLOWLIST: One exported constant beside NGRACE_CHANGE_COMPANION_TAGS maps bundle filename to root tag to validator, and grammar.ts:751, :798 and :809 all read it (A11.1). A bundle carrying run-ledger.xml, run.xml and a run/ directory produces no change.unexpected-file for any of them. The near neighbours still error: notes.xml inside a bundle, a stray spec.old.xml, and a .xml file directly under changes/active (grammar.ts:737-739). Both directions reported per A7.2 — this is a detection-boundary change.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-LEDGER-GRAMMAR: validateRunLedgerArtifact rejects, each with its own code and its own unit test: unknown root tag, identity absent or not one canonical C-*, identity disagreeing with the bundle directory, non-monotonic epoch numbers, a renumbered or reordered epoch, an event ID outside every allocation, a hole inside a used range, and a used range with no terminal event (ledger.* codes per A11.3). Eight tests minimum; a single "invalid ledger" test is not evidence. Modelled on validateChangeDesignContextArtifact (grammar.ts:575).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CURSOR-CONDITIONAL: Three behaviours, one integration test each. No run.xml: silent, no issue of any kind (D1) — write this one first, it is the behaviour the house's fail-closed instinct loses. run.xml naming a task absent from plan.xml: cursor.unknown-task, error. run.xml consistent with plan.xml: clean. A fourth test covers what cursor.unknown-task cannot: a cursor copied from another bundle whose task IDs collide is caught by cursor.bundle-id-mismatch, not by unknown-task (A11.4).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RUN-DIR-UNWALKED: A malformed or garbage .xml file under run/ produces no lint issue, pinned by a test that says so (A11.2). The test exists so the absence is a decision on the record rather than an artifact of the isFile() filter at grammar.ts:808.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-WRITE-SURFACE: cursor show and bare cursor regenerate leave the tree byte-identical, proven by directory snapshot using the shared snapshotProjectTree (test-support/fixtures.ts:194) — not by copying the private helper at scale-ergonomics.test.ts:66 (A10.7). regenerate writes only under --apply, following ngrace graph split: dirty-worktree guard (grace-graph.ts:110), dryRun: !options.apply (:165), early return (:169), and a dry-run notice (:297). grep -rn 'writeFileSync\|mkdirSync' src --include='*.ts' | grep -v test returns the A10.9 baseline plus src/grace-cursor.ts and nothing else. Output reported verbatim.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-FOLD-ORDERING: A failure injected between write and delete leaves both the ledger and the loose files, and a follow-up fold is idempotent rather than duplicating the epoch. The delete step is provably unreachable before the verify step (§3.7 gate 4). A concurrent-append test with two allocations and interleaved writes folds successfully with every event present, and no ordering assertion anywhere refers to a clock (§0.2, §3.7 gate 3).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-REGENERATE-SOURCES:
Amended by A13.2 — the original text named ObservedWriteScope for a task-level answer it cannot give: the scope is bundle-level (scope.ts:279, :405) and no plan task carries a file list (TASK_REQUIRED_SECTIONS, grammar.ts:48). Correction 26.
Regeneration reads ledger, then loose run/ events, then repository evidence, and labels row 3 output inferred. Row 3 sets state to in-progress when the bundle's ObservedWriteScope intersects the repository's changed files (observedWriteScopeContains, scope.ts:91, against the changed set collectObservedDrift already computes) and idle when it does not; sets task to the absence value with a reason, never a task id; leaves epoch absent; and marks the change complete only when --assertion-mode target evaluates the plan's TargetAssertions clean. It runs no commands: per-task Verification/Command is rejected because it requires execution, MustPassCommand is deliberately skipped under default lint (A5.2), and §0.2 forbids tests depending on an external toolchain.
Returning the plan's first task as the position is deleted — it is a confident false position (A12.1) with no evidence at any granularity.
Tests: one proves an inferred row is distinguishable from a ledger-derived row in both text and JSON output; one proves a project with a ledger and no loose events regenerates identically from rows 1-2 alone; one constructs a bundle whose ObservedWriteScope files are genuinely modified and asserts state in-progress with task carrying the absence value; one constructs an untouched bundle and asserts idle. Reverting the row-3 branch must fail the last two — that is the §0.7.2 evidence whose absence made correction 24 invisible. Row 3 must never populate the fields D1 lists as unrecoverable.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-RECOVER-NOT-BLOCK: cursor show never blocks. A missing cursor, an identity-less cursor and a mismatched cursor all take the same code path: distrust, re-derive, announce. The announcement uses the verdict vocabulary in skills/ngrace/ngrace-cli/references/verdicts.md and introduces no second vocabulary (A11.5, anti-pattern 9 and 5). lint still errors on the written file — the two surfaces disagree by design, and one test asserts exactly that pairing.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-STATUS-SURFACE: ngrace status prints epoch and task counts, and prints normally when no cursor exists. The change identity and the next skill already ship (formatStatusText:333, chooseNextAction:171-184) and are not re-credited to this phase. chooseNextAction does not consult the cursor: a project whose cursor implies a different position than plan state still gets the plan-derived nextAction, asserted by test (A10.8, anti-pattern 7).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DROP-SITE-INVENTORY: The A5.4 drop-site inventory for ChangeBundleStatus and StatusResult in the phase report, each site file:line marked widened, deliberately not widened with reason, or not on the path. formatStatusText:333 re-lists five fields by name and is the site most likely to drop the new epoch field — JSON carrying it while text silently does not would be corrections 2, 9 and 10 a fourth time. addNgraceIssue (lint/core.ts:54-62) still re-copies five fields; nothing in this phase may reintroduce a dependency on it carrying more.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-CATALOG-REGISTRATION: All twelve codes are exact catalog entries with derivedFrom and proposedBy (catalog.ts:22-26, §12.1). None carries issueClass "absence" (A11.3). Each has at least one integration test proving it fires and at least one proving it does not fire on a clean project (§0.2).
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-GRAPH-COVERAGE: M-CURSOR (src/grace-cursor.ts), M-ARTIFACT-TYPES (src/artifact/types.ts) and M-CLI (src/grace.ts) exist in .ngrace/graph/main.xml with matching V-M-* verification entries, so every src file this change edits has an owning module (A11.7). bun run validate:ci, bun run validate:packed and bun run ngrace lint --path . green.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ADDITIVE: Invariant 5 demonstrated, not asserted: polyglotFixture(), minimalTsFixture(), scaleFixture(20), examples/ and bun run ngrace lint --path . each yield zero new codes (§0.7.4, A9). A new error on a previously-green project is release-breaking; do not edit a fixture to suit a check.
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-DOCS-AND-SKILLS: The sixth subcommand reaches its callers: README.md's command table and output-format list, skills/ngrace/ngrace-cli/SKILL.md's surface list, and skills/ngrace/ngrace-execute/SKILL.md stating when to advance and fold — one or two sentences, never restating codes the binary emits (D13, anti-pattern 10). Both packaged mirrors byte-identical in the same commit (A10.6, §12.2). Token delta reported (§0.5, D15).

VerificationIntent.ExpectedCommand: bun test src/grace-cursor.test.ts src/artifact/grammar.test.ts src/grace-lint.test.ts src/grace-status.test.ts
VerificationIntent.ExpectedEvidence: The A7.2 both-directions table for the grammar.ts:809 boundary, naming what newly passes and what still errors. The A5.4 drop-site inventory for ChangeBundleStatus and StatusResult. The write-surface grep output verbatim against the A10.9 baseline. The interrupted-fold and re-fold-idempotent outputs. The concurrent-append test with no clock reference. Proof that a cursor copied between bundles is caught by bundle-id-mismatch and not by unknown-task, with the colliding task IDs shown. An inferred row distinguishable from a ledger-derived row in both output formats. The §0.7.4 sweep across all five targets. The mutation-check table with no zero rows, or the discriminating negative added for each. The adversarial probe covering the five track-specific categories in §0.7.3.

Assumptions.Assumption: §3.2 preconditions re-measured at 7388d5e, not assumed (A10.1): the evidence bundle is complete and archived; NGRACE_CHANGE_COMPANION_TAGS is live at artifact/types.ts:28, consumed at grammar.ts:11 and :26; validateChangeDesignContextArtifact is at grammar.ts:575, not the :574 the plan cites.

A10's corrections 16-23 and A11's five decisions govern where they disagree with §3.4 and §3.5. Step 3.5.1's verify check as written names change.invalid-root-tag, which grammar.ts:499 cannot emit for this input, and is replaced per A10.3.

The write-surface baseline at 7388d5e is grace-graph.ts:3, :289, :291 and the dart adapter's temp-dir use at adapters/dart.ts:2, :178 — nothing else (A10.9). Re-measure before claiming the post-state.
Path-only modules without LINKS remain warning-level and deliberate; the eight existing graph.module-without-linked-files warnings are the expected clean state.
